summary: This version of RobotPet guards the battery level so it can never be charged above 100% or drained below 0%. A property and its setter intercept every read and write of `pet.battery`, clamping any unsafe value before it is stored.

lines.code: self.battery = battery  # uses the property setter for validation
lines.text: Even inside the constructor, this assignment is routed through the setter, so a pet created with a battery of 120 or -40 is corrected before the object ever exists.
The `@property` decorator turns the method below it into an attribute-style read, which is why the printing code still says `pet1.battery` with no parentheses.
The real value now lives in `_battery`, and the leading underscore is Python's convention for "internal, do not touch directly."
This pairs a write handler with the property, so every `pet.battery = ...` anywhere in the program must pass through the validation below.
Rather than raising an error, the setter clamps an over-charge back to the safe maximum, which keeps the battery inside 0-100 no matter what a caller asks for.
Methods inside the class use the public `self.battery` too, so they always read the validated value instead of reaching for `_battery`.
